questions.stem: Study group: tree has P(rain)=0.3 then P(umbrella|rain)=0.8; P(rain and umbrella)?
questions.explanation: Multiply along branches: 0.3*0.8=0.24. Adding is wrong.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.2, P(B)=0.3, disjoint; P(A or B)?
questions.explanation: Disjoint: P(A or B)=0.2+0.3=0.5. Subtracting overlap is wrong (none).

questions.stem: Study group: independent P(A)=0.4, P(B)=0.5; P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: Independent: 0.4*0.5=0.2. Adding is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.5, P(B)=0.4, P(A and B)=0.2; independent?
questions.explanation: Independence iff P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B). Here 0.2=0.2, yes. Magnitude or disjoint confusion wrong.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.learningObjective: Use complement to find at least one
questions.stem: Study group: P(success)=0.2 per trial, 3 trials independent; P(at least one success)?
questions.explanation: 1 - (0.8)^3 = 1-0.512=0.488. Direct summing can double count.

questions.stem: Study group: which condition is NOT required for binomial?

options.text: Sample must be drawn without replacement from finite population
Probability of success must be constant

questions.explanation: Binomial requires independent trials with constant p and fixed n. Without replacement is hypergeometric.

questions.stem: Study group: n=4, p=0.5; P(X=2)?
questions.explanation: C(4,2)*0.5^2*0.5^2 = 6*0.0625=0.375. Forgetting combination gives 0.0625.

questions.stem: Study group tree: P(A)=0.6, P(B|A)=0.5, P(B|A')=0.2; P(B)?
questions.explanation: Law of total probability: 0.3+0.08=0.38. Ignoring branch is wrong.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: can two events with positive probabilities be both disjoint and independent?

options.text: No, disjoint positive events are dependent

questions.explanation: If disjoint and positive, P(A∩B)=0≠P(A)P(B), so dependent. Yes always is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.3, P(B|A)=0.4; P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B|A)=0.3*0.4=0.12. Multiplying marginals ignores dependence.

questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.5, P(B)=0.4, P(A and B)=0.2; P(B|A)?
questions.explanation: P(B|A)=0.2/0.5=0.4=P(B), so independent. Using 0.2/0.4=0.5 is wrong.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.stem: Study group: P(at least one of A,B) shortcut using complement?
questions.explanation: At least one complement is neither: 1-P(A'∩B'). 1-P(A)-P(B) is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: flipping a coin until first heads; is this binomial?

options.text: No, number of trials not fixed

questions.explanation: Geometric (until first success) has random n, not binomial. Coin flips alone don't suffice.

questions.stem: Study group: n=5, p=0.3; P(X=2)?
Study group tree: P(A)=0.4, P(B|A)=0.5, P(B|A')=0.2; P(A|B)? (Bayes) approximate.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.5, P(B)=0.4, P(A and B)=0.2; P(A or B)?
questions.explanation: P(A∪B)=0.5+0.4-0.2=0.7. Adding without subtracting overlap gives 0.9.

questions.stem: Study group: P(A∩B∩C)=? for dependent events.
questions.explanation: Chain rule conditions each on previous. Assuming independence is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: coin flip and die roll; are they independent?
questions.explanation: Separate experiments are independent. Same probability not required.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.stem: Study group: P(defect)=0.1 per item, 5 independent; P(at least one defect)?
Study group: drawing with replacement from box; binomial?
questions.explanation: With replacement, trials independent with constant p, so binomial. Finite population alone not issue.

questions.stem: Study group: n=3, p=0.5; P(X<=1)?
questions.explanation: P(0)+P(1)=0.125+0.375=0.5. Using P(1) only is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group tree: P(first heads)=0.5, then P(second tails|heads)=0.5; P(H then T)?
questions.explanation: 0.5*0.5=0.25. Adding gives 1, wrong.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: if A,B disjoint, P(A or B)=?
questions.explanation: Disjoint intersection zero, so sum. General formula reduces to sum. Multiplying is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: P(first red)=0.4, P(second red|first red)=0.3; P(both red)?
questions.explanation: 0.4*0.3=0.12. Multiplying 0.4*0.4 ignores dependence.

questions.stem: Study group table: P(A)=0.5,P(B)=0.4,P(A∩B)=0.15; independent?
questions.explanation: Product 0.2 ≠ 0.15, dependent. Closeness or magnitude is wrong.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.stem: Study group: P(rain)=0.3; P(no rain)?
questions.explanation: Complement = 1-0.3=0.7. Squaring is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: rolling a die and counting sixes; binomial?
questions.explanation: Success/failure dichotomy suffices even with multiple failure outcomes. p need not be 0.5.

questions.stem: Study group: n=4, p=0.25; P(X=0)?
questions.explanation: (0.75)^4=0.3164. Using 1-... is complement.

questions.stem: Study group tree: two paths to B have probs 0.12 and 0.08; P(B)?
questions.explanation: Sum path probs 0.12+0.08=0.2. Multiplying paths is wrong.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: explain why P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B) when mutually exclusive.

answer.exemplar: Mutually exclusive means A and B cannot both occur, so intersection probability is zero. Thus general addition rule reduces to sum of individual probabilities.

questions.explanation: Intersection zero eliminates overlap term. Adding overlap would double count.

questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.6, P(B|A)=0.5; P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: 0.6*0.5=0.3. Multiplying by P(B) marginal is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: drawing without replacement; are draws independent?

options.text: No, because first draw changes composition

questions.explanation: Without replacement, conditional probabilities change, so dependent. Large population is approximation only.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.stem: Study group: P(at least one failure) shortcut?
questions.explanation: At least one failure complement is all successes. 1-P(all failures) is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: which is a binomial condition?
questions.explanation: Binomial requires independent trials. Mutually exclusive or varying p is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: n=10, p=0.3; expected number of successes?
questions.explanation: Mean = np = 10*0.3=3. Using n*p*(1-p) is variance.

questions.stem: Study group tree: P(A)=0.5, P(B|A)=0.4, P(C|A∩B)=0.5; P(A∩B∩C)?
questions.explanation: 0.5*0.4*0.5=0.1. Adding is wrong.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: disjoint A,B with P(A)=0.2,P(B)=0.3; P(at most one)?
questions.explanation: Disjoint means cannot both occur, so at most one always, probability 1. Using 0.5 is P(exactly one).

questions.stem: Study group: independent P(A)=0.25, P(B)=0.4; P(A and B)?
Study group: independent P(A)=0.3, P(B)=0.4; P(A|B)?
questions.explanation: For independent, P(A|B)=P(A)=0.3. Using P(A∩B)/P(B)=0.12/0.4=0.3 same.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.stem: Study group: P(at least 2 successes in 3) shortcut?
questions.explanation: At least 2 complement is 0 or 1 success. Direct sum not shortcut. 1-P(3) wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: surveying 50 voters about candidate preference; binomial?
questions.explanation: Sampling without replacement from finite population is hypergeometric, approximately binomial if large. Exactly binomial is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: n=3, p=0.4; P(X=3)?
questions.explanation: 0.4^3=0.064. Multiplying by combination (1) same; using 3*0.4 is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group tree: P(path)=0.15; P(not path)?
questions.explanation: Complement = 1-0.15=0.85. Squaring is wrong.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: disjoint P(A)=0.35, P(B)=0.25; P(A or B)?
questions.explanation: 0.35+0.25=0.6. Subtracting overlap wrong (none).

questions.stem: Study group: independent P(A)=0.5, P(B)=0.6; P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: 0.5*0.6=0.3. Adding gives 1.1 invalid.

questions.stem: Study group asks equation for independence of A and B.
questions.explanation: Independence iff joint equals product. Disjoint equation is different.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.stem: Study group: P(event)=0.15; P(complement)?
Study group: which scenario is binomial?

options.text: Draw cards without replacement count aces
10 flips of a fair coin, count heads

questions.explanation: 10 coin flips: fixed n, constant p, independent, two outcomes. Others fail conditions.

questions.stem: Study group: n=8, p=0.25; variance of X?
questions.explanation: Variance = np(1-p)=8*0.25*0.75=1.5. Using np=2 is mean.

questions.stem: Study group tree: P(first heads)=0.5, P(second heads|first heads)=0.6, P(second heads|first tails)=0.3; P(second heads)?

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: when must you subtract P(A and B) in addition rule?
questions.explanation: Subtract intersection when events overlap. Always or never is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.7, P(B|A)=0.2; P(A and B)?
questions.explanation: 0.7*0.2=0.14. Multiplying by P(B) marginal is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: if P(B|A)=P(B), then A and B are?
questions.explanation: Equal conditional and marginal implies independence. Disjoint/complementary is wrong.

questions.topic: A complement used as a shortcut
questions.learningObjective: Complement of at least one failure
questions.stem: Study group: P(failure)=0.2 per trial, 4 trials; P(at least one failure)?
Study group: if p changes across trials, distribution is not binomial; what is it?
questions.explanation: Varying p violates binomial condition; Poisson binomial applies. Averaging p is wrong.

questions.stem: Study group: n=4, p=0.5; P(X<=2)?
Study group tree: P(A)=0.45; P(A')?
questions.explanation: 1-0.45=0.55. Squaring is wrong.

questions.topic: The addition rule for disjoint events
questions.stem: Study group: disjoint A,B with P(A)=0.2,P(B)=0.3; P(exactly one)?
questions.explanation: Disjoint so exactly one = A or B = 0.5. P(A)+P(B)-2P(both)=0.5.

questions.stem: Study group: P(A)=0.5, P(B|A)=0.4, P(C|A∩B)=0.3; P(A∩B∩C)?
questions.explanation: 0.5*0.4*0.3=0.06. Adding is wrong.
